record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For fourth-order degenerate thin-film equations for a nonnegative film height h, when the film has compact support and the equation degenerates as h approaches zero at a moving contact line, what boundary conditions should be imposed at the edge of the support so that the contact-line problem is physically and mathematically well posed?

evidence.quote: it is unclear what boundary conditions are required at the edge of the support.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fourth-order degenerate thin-film equation
  h_t + (m(h) h_{xxx})_x = 0,    x ∈ Ω(t) ⊂ ℝ, t > 0,
for a nonnegative film height h(x,t) ≥ 0, where the mobility m(h) ≥ 0 vanishes at h = 0 (typical examples include m(h) = h^n with n > 0, derived from the lubrication approximation of surface-tension-driven flow of a thin viscous film on a solid substrate). Assume the film has compact support so that Ω(t) = {x : h(x,t) > 0} is a bounded open set, and let the moving contact line be the boundary ∂Ω(t) where h = 0 and the equation degenerates.

Determine which boundary conditions must be imposed at the moving contact line ∂Ω(t) (in addition to h = 0 there) so that the resulting free-boundary problem is both physically meaningful (consistent with the underlying fluid-mechanical model of a contact line on a solid substrate, including treatment of the classical no-slip stress singularity) and mathematically well posed (admitting a unique solution depending continuously on the data, in an appropriate class of nonnegative weak or classical solutions). In particular, specify a complete set of contact-line conditions (e.g. prescribing the contact angle |h_x|, a kinematic law for the speed of ∂Ω(t), or a flux condition) that yields a well-posed evolution for general mobilities m(h) and general wetting regimes (complete and partial wetting).
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of the correct contact-line boundary conditions for degenerate fourth-order thin-film equations remains an active research area, but substantial partial progress has been made. Well-posedness has been established in several regimes: with prescribed contact angle h=0, |h_x|=const in partial wetting (Knüpfer, Giacomelli–Knüpfer–Otto, Gnann and collaborators) and for the perfect-wetting (zero contact angle) regime (e.g. Gnann–Petrache 2023/2025) for broad classes of mobilities. A fully general, physically and mathematically definitive prescription valid across all mobility exponents and wetting regimes, including slippage models, is not yet complete.

status_evidence.title: Well-Posedness for a Class of Thin-Film Equations with General Mobility in the Regime of Partial Wetting
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes well-posedness with boundary conditions h=0, |h_x|=1 at the free boundary for a general class of mobilities in partial wetting.
status_evidence.claim: Partial-wetting contact-line problem is well posed under a prescribed nonzero contact-angle condition for general mobilities.

status_evidence.title: Classical solutions to the thin-film equation with general mobility in the perfect-wetting regime
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs classical solutions in the zero-contact-angle (perfect wetting) regime for general mobility exponents.
status_evidence.claim: The perfect-wetting case admits classical contact-line solutions, addressing well-posedness there.

status_evidence.title: Strong solutions and stability for a thin-film equation of shear-thinning fluids with contact line in partial wetting
status_evidence.snippet: Recent extension to non-Newtonian (shear-thinning) thin-film equations with partial-wetting contact line conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Research on contact-line boundary conditions and well-posedness remains ongoing in 2026.

status_evidence.title: Viscous Thin Films (MPI MIS)
status_evidence.snippet: Describes ongoing program studying well-posedness and regularity for thin-film free-boundary problems with various contact-line conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Generalization across all mobility exponents and a unified picture including slippage is still being developed.
